steps.title: Customer authorizes the integration and selects pages in the page picker
steps.detail: Direct a test customer to the connection's authorization URL from the Configuration tab. The customer selects only the test pages to share in the page picker and clicks Allow access. Notion redirects to the redirect URI with a temporary code parameter. Expected output: a redirect URL containing code. No token request is made here.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URL contains a code parameter, and the customer has shared only the representative test pages.

evidence.quote: 1 The user visits the connection’s authorization URL. Find this URL in the Configuration tab of your connection in the Developer portal.
3 The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.
4 After the user approves, Notion redirects them to your redirect URI with a temporary authorization code.

fields: Authorization URL: copied from the Configuration tab of the connection
Page picker selection: test pages chosen by the customer, not real rollout pages
Redirect code: temporary code query parameter from the redirect

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for a customer access token
steps.detail: The developer's backend sends the temporary code to the token endpoint using HTTP Basic authentication with CLIENT_ID:CLIENT_SECRET. Expected output: a JSON body with access_token, refresh_token, bot_id, and workspace_id. Store the token pair securely per customer. No resource request is run in this step.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token and workspace_id, and the token is stored securely for the authorizing customer.

evidence.quote: Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token .
The request is authorized using HTTP Basic Authentication. The credential is a colon-delimited combination of the connection’s CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET , like so:
"access_token" string An access token used to authorize requests to the Notion API. ✅

fields: REDIRECT_CODE: code query parameter from the customer's redirect
REDIRECT_URI: must match the redirect URI configured in the portal
Client credentials: from the Configuration tab

steps.title: Read a shared page's title through the page retrieve endpoint
steps.detail: Read-only GET of one customer-shared page using the customer's access token: GET https://api.notion.com/v1/pages/<SHARED_PAGE_ID> with header Notion-Version: 2026-03-11. Expected output: a page object whose properties.title.title array contains the page title. This read does not create or modify the page. Pagination is not required for this single-object read. Boundary check: confirm the page is one the customer shared, then inspect the actual grant and outgoing request log if a read is denied. 403 means the connection lacks the Read content capability. 404 means a missing page or missing access, so it does not by itself prove authorization. Make no write calls.
steps.doneWhen: The response has object page, the title text is in properties.title.title, and no write endpoint was called.

evidence.quote: Pages that aren't in a data source always return only title .
Read content : This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
Authorization : Bearer {INTEGRATION_TOKEN}

fields: SHARED_PAGE_ID: test page ID the customer selected in the page picker
CUSTOMER_ACCESS_TOKEN: access_token from the token exchange response
Title: properties.title.title in the response

steps.title: Read a shared page's content as Markdown
steps.detail: Read-only GET of the same shared test page as markdown using the customer's access token: GET https://api.notion.com/v1/pages/<SHARED_PAGE_ID>/markdown?markdown_version=v2 with header Notion-Version: 2026-03-11. Expected output: a markdown body with the page content. If unknown blocks appear, their truncated and unknown_block_ids fields identify them for a follow-up fetch by block ID, which is also a read. Pagination is not required for this read. Boundary check: the connection needs Read content capability on the target page. 403 means the capability is missing and 404 means a missing page or missing access, so inspect the actual grant and request log instead of inferring authorization.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains the page markdown with the expected test content, and no write endpoint was called.

evidence.quote: --url https://api.notion.com/v1/pages/{page_id}/markdown \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
Headers ​ Notion-Version enum<string>
If your connection is reading data to export it out of Notion, your connection will only need Read content capabilities.

fields: SHARED_PAGE_ID: same test page ID as the prior step
CUSTOMER_ACCESS_TOKEN: access_token from the token exchange response
markdown_version=v2: recommended Notion-flavored Markdown

steps.title: Confirm a page the customer did not share is not readable
steps.detail: Send a read request for a test page that exists in the customer's workspace but was not selected in the page picker. Expected output: HTTP 404 object_not_found, showing the grant limits reads to shared pages. This is a nonmutating boundary check; it does not test a nonexistent ID.
steps.doneWhen: The unshared page returns 404 and the shared page from the earlier step still returns 200.

fields: UNSHARED_PAGE_ID: existing test page not selected in the picker
Expected result: 404 for missing access
Capability check: Read content only, so no write behavior is tested
